_: What the account's sound library asks ElevenLabs for (soundlib.mjs gen, a paid call per take, only on the person's word), and what build keeps. One entry a sound: id <group>/<name>; kind hit (a one-shot, trimmed to its onset), swell (grows to a point: the mixer can put that point on the cue) or bed (a long background, looped); is: what it is the sound of; prompt: the text sent; seconds; candidates: takes asked; keep: takes kept; use: what it is for (pick a sound by its use); slice: a tiny one-shot asked as several seconds of the same thing and cut into single events; loop: asked as a seamless loop; min/max: the length a kept take must have; minCentroid: how bright it must be (Hz); repeat: meant to run in a row (a counter); note: what to know before using it; tags: AudioSet labels (the AST model's own names) any one of which, heard at 0.05 or more, keeps a take; accept: other entries whose description CLAP may hear a take as and still keep it; reject: AudioSet labels that, heard at 0.1 or more, throw a take out; musical: a sound meant to carry a pitch, so a take heard as music is not thrown out; maxrank: how near its own description must rank among all (default 5); rev: the prompt was rewritten, so its new takes get new raw names. A sound the library lacks is a new entry here, then gen --only <id> and build --only <id>.

sounds.is: a single computer mouse click
sounds.prompt: A computer mouse clicked five times, slowly, one single click and then a pause. Close-mic, dry, no reverb, no music.
sounds.use: a pointer presses a button

sounds.prompt: A fingertip tapping a glass phone screen five times, slowly, soft dull taps with a pause after each. Close-mic, dry, no reverb, no music.
